source.title: Doubling constructions: Global functoriality for non-generic cuspidal representations
source.authors: Yuanqing Cai, Solomon Friedberg and Eyal Kaplan
source.version: arXiv v5, 20 May 2024, 60 pages, the version to be published in the Annals (arXiv comment); the Annals site gives pp. 893–966 but its PDF was not fetched. Numbering from v5; Unpaywall lists only v5 (also mirrored by Hokkaido University).

summary: Cai, Friedberg and Kaplan prove that every irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of a split symplectic, special orthogonal or general spin group over a number field has a weak functorial transfer to GL_N (Theorem 0.1), without genericity and independently of the trace formula. They apply the converse theorem, controlling the twisted L-functions with the generalized doubling method: local poles in Re(s) ≥ 1/2 are attained by the doubling integrals through Kaplan's GL_c × GL_k integrals (Theorem 3.12, Appendix A), the doubling Eisenstein series is holomorphic away from twisted self-duality (Theorem 4.1), and so the twisted L-functions are entire (Theorem 4.8). They deduce that weak transfers are coarse transfers at every place and that local coarse transfers exist. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and one finding is recorded (a unitarity hypothesis in §3.6, repaired by a twist). Not formalised.

items.name: The split groups G_l and the embedding r_G
items.statement: G_l is Sp_l (l even), SO_l or GSpin_l split over F; GSpin_l is the split group with the based root datum of §1. Standard Levi subgroups M ≅ M_β × G_{l−2r} are fixed by i_M, Υ_l is the character of GSpin_l with kernel Spin_l, and r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) is the natural embedding (Ĝ = SO_{2n+1}, SO_{2n}, Sp_{2n}, GSO_{2n}, GSp_{2n}).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Rankin–Selberg γ-, L- and ε-factors for GL_l × GL_r
items.statement: The γ-, L- and ε-factors of Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika and Jacquet–Shalika for pairs of irreducible admissible representations of GL_l and GL_r over a local field, defined also for non-generic representations ([JPSS83, §9.4]).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Satake parametrization of unramified representations
items.statement: An unramified π ∈ Irr(G) over a non-archimedean field is parametrized by a semisimple conjugacy class [t_π] in Ĝ.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Unramified and archimedean functorial transfer T(π)
items.statement: For unramified π over a non-archimedean field, T(π) is the unramified Π ∈ Irr(GL_N) with Satake class [r_G(t_π)]; over an archimedean field, T(π) is parametrized by r_G ∘ φ, where φ is the Langlands parameter of π ([Lan89]). The central character of T(π) is χ_π^{N/2}.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Weak functorial transfer
items.statement: Π on GL_N(A) is a weak functorial transfer of an irreducible automorphic π of G(A) if at almost all finite places where π_ν is unramified, Π_ν is the local unramified transfer of π_ν via r_G, and at the infinite places the infinitesimal character of Π_ν is determined via r_G by that of π_ν.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Generalized Speh representations and (k, c) models
items.statement: For unitary τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), ρ_c(τ) is the unique irreducible quotient of the representation of GL_kc induced from (τ ⊗ … ⊗ τ)δ^{1/(2k)}; in general it is defined through the Langlands data of τ. (k^c) is the unique maximal orbit of its wave-front set, dim Hom_{U_(c^k)}(ρ_c(τ), ψ_k) = 1, and W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) is its unique (k, c) model.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: The local generalized doubling integral
items.statement: With H = G_2kc, the Siegel parabolic P, the unipotent U with character ψ_U generic for ((2k−1)^c 1^c), the embedding e: G × G → St(ψ_U), δ = δ_0δ_1 and the involution ι of §3.3, and an entire section f of Ind_P^H(|·|^{s−1/2}χ_π W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) ⊗ χ_π), the integral is Z(s, ω, f) = ∫_{C°_G\G} ∫_{U_0} ω(g) f(s, δu_0 e_2(ιg)) ψ_U(u_0) du_0 dg for a matrix coefficient ω of π^∨.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Basic properties of the local doubling integral
items.statement: Z(s, ω, f) converges absolutely in Re(s) ≫ 0 independently of the data, continues meromorphically as a continuous trilinear form on V(s, τ, c) × π × (π^ι)^∨, and for each s some ω and K_H-finite f make it finite and nonzero near s. For unramified normalized data it equals L(s, π × τ)/b(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π) with b as in (3.3).
items.note: Cited from [CFK22]; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Invariance of the inner u_0-integral
items.statement: In Re(s) ≫ 0, ∫_{U_0} f(s, δu_0 e(g_0, ιg_0)) ψ_U(u_0) du_0 = ∫_{U_0} f(s, δu_0) ψ_U(u_0) du_0 for all f and g_0 ∈ G.
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Corollary 2.3]; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Doubling γ-, L- and ε-factors
items.statement: γ(s, π × τ, ψ) is defined by the functional equation (3.6) with the normalized intertwining operator M* and the factor ϑ of (3.7). L and ε are defined from γ for tempered data (P(q^{−s})^{−1} from the zeros of γ; archimedean via T(π)), by twisting for essentially tempered data, and through the Langlands quotient σ ⋊ π′ by (3.17): L(s, π × τ) = L(s, σ × τ)L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ)∏_j L(s, π′ × τ_j).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Characterization of the doubling γ-factor
items.statement: For π ∈ Irr(G) and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), γ(s, π × τ, ψ) satisfies and is characterized by unramified twisting (3.8), multiplicativity (3.9)–(3.10), the unramified formula L(1 − s, π^∨ × τ^∨)/L(s, π × τ), duality, the functional equation (3.11), the dependence on ψ (3.12), the archimedean property (3.13) and the crude global functional equation (3.14).
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Theorem 4.2]; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Compatibility with the unramified and archimedean transfer
items.statement: For π ∈ Irr(G) and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), with π unramified if F is non-archimedean, the γ-, L- and ε-factors of π × τ and T(π) × τ coincide.
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Lemma 7.1] in the non-archimedean case; (3.13) otherwise; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Holomorphy of tempered L-factors
items.statement: For tempered π ∈ Irr(G) (unramified if F is non-archimedean) and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k): if τ is tempered, L(s, π × τ) is holomorphic in Re(s) > 0; if τ is unitary, it is holomorphic in Re(s) ≥ 1/2.
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Corollary 7.2]; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Poles of L(s, π × τ) in Re(s) ≥ 1/2 for a Langlands quotient
items.statement: If τ and χ_π are unitary, π is unramified when F is non-archimedean, and π is the Langlands quotient of σ ⋊ π′ as in (3.16) with l > 0, then L(s, π × τ)/L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ) is holomorphic and nonzero in Re(s) ≥ 1/2.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Stability of γ-factors
items.statement: Over a non-archimedean F, let π ∈ Irr(G) and Π ∈ Irr(GL_N) with central character χ_π^{N/2}. If η is a sufficiently highly ramified character (depending on π and Π), then for every unramified τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) the γ-, L- and ε-factors of π × ητ and Π × ητ coincide, and L(s, π × ητ) = L(s, Π × ητ) = 1.
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Lemma 7.3]; Remark 3.11 removes the unramified and generic assumptions on Π; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Coarse transfer
items.statement: Π ∈ Irr(GL_N) is a coarse transfer of π ∈ Irr(G) if γ(s, π × τ, ψ) = γ(s, Π × τ, ψ) for every k ≥ 1 and every τ ∈ Irr(GL_k) (3.18); by multiplicativity it suffices to check supercuspidal τ.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Gauge bound for (k, c) Whittaker functions
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), k > 1, there is d_0 > 0 such that for every W ∈ W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) there is φ ∈ S(Mat_c) with |W(diag(g, I_(k−1)c))| ≤ |det g|^{−d_0} φ(g) for all g ∈ GL_c.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Archimedean bounds for (k, c) functionals
items.statement: Over an archimedean field there are d_0 > 0 and a continuous seminorm γ with |λ(ρ_c(τ)(ugo)ξ)| ≤ γ(ξ)|τ((det g_k)I_k)| ∏_{i<k} |det(g_k^{−1}g_i)|^{−d_0} for g = diag(g_1, …, g_k), and, for each ξ, the refined bound (3.20) with Schwartz functions φ_i of g_{i+1}^{−1}g_i.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: The functional T and descent from (k, c) to (k, l) models
items.statement: For unitary τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), T(W, µ) = ∫_{U_R} W(r_z)µ(z) dz converges absolutely and defines a continuous functional on W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) ⊗ S^lin(U_R); a ↦ T(m_a·W ⊗ µ) maps onto the functions a ↦ W_l(m′_a) with W_l in |·|^{(kc−kl−c+l)/2}W_ψ(ρ_l(τ)).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: The GL_l × GL_k reduction integral Z^2
items.statement: For σ ∈ Irr(GL_l) (unramified if F is non-archimedean) and unitary τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), the integral (3.32) converges in Re(s) ≫ 0, continues meromorphically and continuously, and for each s some data with compactly supported φ and µ make Z^2/L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ) nonzero at s.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Z^1 as an integral over the open cell
items.statement: When absolutely convergent, Z^1(s, ω, f) of (3.40) equals the integral (3.41) over U_R × C°_G\U_{R′}R′^− × U_R^− × U_0 × GL_l, through an open embedding U into U_{P′} that is a homeomorphism (diffeomorphism) onto its image.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Nonvanishing of Z^1 modulo L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ)
items.statement: For π ∈ Irr_rel(G) written as in (3.16) and unitary τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), for every s_0 there are data with Z^1 absolutely convergent in Re(s) ≫ 0, meromorphic, and Z^1/L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ) nonzero at s_0.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). See finding E1 on the unitarity of χ_π.

items.name: Archimedean convergence of the unfolded integrals
items.statement: Over an archimedean field, (3.39) and Z^1 converge absolutely in Re(s) ≫ 0 independently of the data and are continuous in ϕ, ϕ^∨ and f.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Nonvanishing of Z modulo L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ)
items.statement: For π ∈ Irr_rel(G) as in (3.16) and unitary τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), for every s there are ω and f with Z(s, ω, f)/L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ) nonzero at s.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). See finding E1 on the unitarity of χ_π.

items.name: Convergence of intertwining integrals against smooth vectors
items.statement: For tempered σ ∈ Irr(M_R) and ν in the positive chamber, ∫_{U_R^−} |⟨ϕ(u), w⟩_σ| du < ∞ for all ϕ ∈ V_R^G(ν, σ) and all (smooth) w, and the pairing is continuous.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Local poles are attained by the doubling integral
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G) be unramified (or F archimedean) with χ_π unitary, and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) unitary. For each s with Re(s) ≥ 1/2 there are ω and a K_H-finite f such that Z(s, ω, f)/L(s, π × τ) is nonzero at s.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Converse Theorem of Cogdell–Kim–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shahidi
items.statement: Let Π = ⊗′Π_ν be irreducible admissible on GL_N(A) with central character trivial on F^* and L(s, Π) absolutely convergent in Re(s) ≫ 0. If for every τ ∈ A(S, η) the L-function L(s, Π × τ) is nice (entire with L(s, Π^∨ × τ^∨), bounded in vertical strips, and satisfying L(s, Π × τ) = ε(s, Π × τ)L(1 − s, Π^∨ × τ^∨)), there is an irreducible automorphic Π′ of GL_N(A) with Π′_ν ≅ Π_ν for all ν ∉ S.
items.note: Cited from [CKPSS01, §2]; A(S, η) is the set of η-twists of unitary cuspidal τ′ of GL_k(A), 1 ≤ k < N, unramified at the nonempty finite set S of finite places.

items.name: The Eisenstein series E_{τ,θ,c}
items.statement: For a cuspidal τ of GL_k(A), H = G_2kc, its Siegel parabolic P and an entire K_H-finite section f of Ind_{P(A)}^{H(A)}((|·|^s ρ_c(τ) ⊗ θ) ∘ i_{M_P}), E_{τ,θ,c}(h; s, f) = Σ_{γ ∈ P(F)\H(F)} f(s, γh), convergent in Re(s) ≫ 0 with meromorphic continuation.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Holomorphy of the intertwining operators M_1 and M_2
items.statement: M_1(s) is holomorphic in Re(s) > −c′/2 and M_2(s) is holomorphic in Re(s) ≥ 1/2.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Shape of the cuspidal exponents
items.statement: Every real part e of a cuspidal exponent of the leading Laurent coefficient E_{s,c} along P_(k^c) has the form Re(s)(a_1, …, a_c) + (b_1, …, b_c) with a_j = ±1 and Σ_{i≤j} b_i ≤ 0 for all j.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Holomorphy of the Eisenstein series
items.statement: For τ unitary cuspidal on GL_k(A) and θ a unitary Hecke character (θ = 1 unless H = GSpin_2kc), if |·|^{it}τ ≇ θτ^∨ for all real t, then E_{τ,θ,c}(h; s, f) is holomorphic in Re(s) ≥ 0.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: The global doubling integral and its Eulerian form
items.statement: For cusp forms ϕ_1 of π and ϕ_2 of π^∨ and an entire K_H-finite section f, Z(s, ϕ_1, ϕ_2, f) integrates ϕ_1(g_1) ιϕ_2(g_2) E^{U,ψ_U}(e(g_1, g_2); s − 1/2, f) over (C°_G(A)G(F) × C°_G(A)G(F))\G(A) × G(A); for decomposable data and a large finite S, b^S(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π) Z(s, ϕ_1, ϕ_2, f) = L^S(s, π × τ) ∏_{ν∈S} Z(s, ω_ν, f_ν) (4.10).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: The completed L-function L(s, π × τ)
items.statement: L(s, π × τ) = ∏_ν L(s, π_ν × τ_ν) and ε(s, π × τ) = ∏_ν ε(s, π_ν × τ_ν, ψ_ν), with the local factors of §3.4.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Global functional equation
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Theorem 8.3]; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Boundedness in vertical strips
items.statement: If L(s, π × τ) and L(1 − s, π^∨ × τ^∨) are entire, they are bounded in vertical strips of finite width.
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Corollary 8.5]; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Entireness of twisted L-functions
items.statement: Let π and τ be unitary cuspidal on G(A) and GL_k(A) with (1) |·|^{it}χ_π τ ≇ τ^∨ for all real t, and (2) L(s, π_ν × τ_ν) = L(s, π_ν^∨ × τ_ν^∨) = 1 at every finite ν where π_ν is not unramified. Then L(s, π × τ) and L(s, π^∨ × τ^∨) are entire and bounded in vertical strips of finite width.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Weak functorial transfer of cuspidal representations
items.statement: Every irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation π of G(A) has a weak functorial transfer Π to GL_N(A); the proof yields one with Π_∞ the archimedean transfer of π_∞ (Remark 4.9).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Weak transfers are coarse transfers everywhere
items.statement: If Π is a weak functorial transfer of a cuspidal π of G(A), then Π_ν is a coarse transfer of π_ν at every place ν.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Existence of local coarse transfers
items.statement: Over a local field f, every π′ ∈ Irr(G(f)) has a coarse transfer to GL_N(f).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: The GL_c × GL_k integrals of Appendix A
items.statement: For π ∈ Irr(GL_c), τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) (k > 1), a matrix coefficient ω of π and W ∈ W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)), Z(s, ω, W) = ∫_{GL_c} W(diag(g, I_(k−1)c)) ω(g) |det g|^{s−(kc−2c+1)/2} dg, with the dual integral Z*(s, ω, W); the γ-factor is defined by γ(s, π × τ, ψ)Z(s, ω, W) = π(−1)^{k−1}Z*(s, ω, W) (A.3).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Uniqueness of the trilinear forms
items.statement: Outside finitely many values of q^{−s} (non-archimedean) or a discrete set of s (archimedean), the space of continuous trilinear forms on π × π^∨ × ρ_c(τ) with the equivariance (A.2) has dimension at most one.
items.note: Cited from [Kap23, Theorem 25].

items.name: Multiplicativity of the appendix γ-factor
items.statement: If π ⊂ Ind_R^G(π_1 ⊗ π_2) for R = R_(l,c−l), then γ(s, π × τ, ψ) = γ(s, π_1 × τ, ψ)γ(s, π_2 × τ, ψ); hence for π unramified or F archimedean it equals the Rankin–Selberg γ-factor.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: The appendix L-factor
items.statement: For π unramified (or F archimedean) and τ unitary generic, there is a nowhere vanishing L(s, π × τ) with L^{−1}Z(s, ω, W) entire for all data and nonzero for suitable data at each s; it can be defined by Z*(1 − s, …), is multiplicative up to entire factors, independent of ψ, and compatible with unramified twists.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: L-factors of Langlands quotients
items.statement: If π is the Langlands quotient of Ind(σ_1 ⊗ … ⊗ σ_d) and π′ that of Ind(σ_2 ⊗ … ⊗ σ_d), then L(s, π′ × τ) = P(s)L(s, π × τ) for an entire P(s) (appendix L-factors).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: The Rankin–Selberg factor divides the appendix L-factor
items.statement: L^{RS}(s, π × τ)^{−1} L(s, π × τ) is entire, where L^{RS} is the Rankin–Selberg factor.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Rankin–Selberg poles are attained by the GL_c × GL_k integrals
items.statement: For π ∈ Irr(GL_c) (unramified if F is non-archimedean) and unitary τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), k > 1, for each s there are ω and W with Z(s, ω, W)/L^{RS}(s, π × τ) nonzero at s; over archimedean fields ω and W can be taken finite.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

routes.title: Automorphic L-functions and local factors, Part II: the generalized doubling method and functorial transfer for classical groups
routes.brief: Automorphic L-functions and local factors, extended to the generalized doubling method of Cai, Friedberg, Ginzburg, Gourevitch and Kaplan for split symplectic, special orthogonal and general spin groups twisted by GL_k. Cover generalized Speh representations and their (k, c) models; the local doubling integrals with their γ-, L- and ε-factors (characterization, compatibility with the unramified and archimedean transfer, stability, holomorphy for tempered data) and the attainment of the poles in Re(s) ≥ 1/2 through the GL_c × GL_k integrals of Kaplan's appendix; the doubling Eisenstein series and its holomorphy away from twisted self-duality; the global integral, functional equation and entireness of twisted L-functions; and the Cogdell–Kim–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shahidi converse theorem. Final theorems: every cuspidal representation of such a group has a weak functorial transfer to GL_N (Theorem 0.1), weak transfers are coarse transfers at every place (Theorem 4.10), and local coarse transfers exist (Corollary 4.11). Import Rankin–Selberg factors from layer AL.3, the Satake isomorphism from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (SR.4), and parabolic induction and Langlands quotients from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.
routes.reason: The doubling integrals, their local factors, the Eisenstein-series analysis and the converse-theorem transfer extend the atlas's automorphic L-function roadmap; its Rankin–Selberg layer AL.3 and the Satake layer SR.4 are imported rather than re-planned.

The proof of Proposition 3.17 applies Lemma 3.16 'for the (k, c) model χ_π W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) = W_ψ(ρ_c(χ_π τ))' and Theorems A.6 and A.11 to χ_π τ.
sourceIssues.correction: Either assume χ_π unitary (π ∈ Irr_rel,a.u.(G), as in Theorem 3.12), or reduce to that case: write χ_π = |·|^r χ_0 with r real and χ_0 unitary. Then W_ψ(ρ_c(χ_π τ)) = |det|^r W_ψ(ρ_c(χ_0 τ)), the factor |det a|^r pulls out of Z^2 because r_z is unipotent, and L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ) = L(s + r, σ^∨ × χ_0 τ).
sourceIssues.reason: Lemma 3.16 (through [CFGK23, §3.2]) and Theorem A.11 are stated for unitary τ, but in Propositions 3.17, 3.19 and Corollary 3.21 the relevant representation is χ_π τ, and χ_π need not be unitary for π ∈ Irr_rel(G) when G = GSpin_c (for Sp_c and SO_c, χ_π = 1). The twist above repairs the argument, and the only use, Theorem 3.12, assumes χ_π unitary, so the main results are unaffected.

summaryBefore: Cai, Friedberg and Kaplan prove that every irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of a symplectic or quasi-split orthogonal group has a weak functorial transfer to GL_N (Theorem 0.1), without assuming genericity. They use the converse theorem, with twisted L-functions controlled by the generalized doubling method (local γ-factors, their stability, and a global analysis of the doubling Eisenstein series). They deduce that the transfer is a coarse transfer at every place, and that local coarse transfers exist. Partial first extraction (cc-442dc5): the main theorems and definitions are items; the remaining lemmas and propositions of §3 and §4 are listed in the handoff.
